# Collective

- By

[![A Serilum Mod. Made with love. Lots of active mods for Fabric, Forge and Neo!](https://cdn.serilum.com/description/header/header.png)](https://www.curseforge.com/linkout?remoteUrl=https%253a%252f%252fserilum.com%252f)

[![CurseForge](https://workflow.serilum.com/badges/svg/curseforge.svg)](https://curseforge.com/members/serilum/projects)[![Modrinth](https://workflow.serilum.com/badges/svg/modrinth.svg)](https://www.curseforge.com/linkout?remoteUrl=https%253a%252f%252fmodrinth.com%252fuser%252fSerilum)[![Patreon](https://workflow.serilum.com/badges/svg/patreon.svg)](https://patreon.com/serilum)[![YouTube](https://workflow.serilum.com/badges/svg/youtube.svg)](https://youtube.com/@serilum)

![About the mod](https://cdn.serilum.com/description/nameplate/about-the-mod.svg)

Collective is a shared library mod with common code for all of Serilum's mods.

It contains data and functions centralized in one place. Collective helps a great deal in maintaining all the Fabric, Forge and NeoForge mod loader versions.

Having access to the library's code environment, creates possibilities for current and future project features. The updating process is also made easier when there's an improvement for a function that is relevant to many others. For example this means having to update one project, instead of six. This saves time and makes me a little happier.

Features:

- Manages all config files and in-game menu of dependent mods. **¹**

- Variables for increased compatibility with other projects.

- Lots of useful functions to prevent code duplication. **²**

- An event to replace and resupply entities.

- Allows toggling the functionality of bundled mods. **³**

- Contains the access transformers/wideners to use private fields. **⁴**

- Networking code to send packets via the Common source set.

- Centralized backwards compatibility for major version changes.

- Optional async update checker for dependent mods that prints to the console.
- And much more! **⁵**

![Description](https://cdn.serilum.com/description/nameplate/description.svg)

**1** \| Because I use the Multiloader template for all of my mods, there is no built-in config I can use from within the Common code. Collective contains a suite of config code that all dependent mods use. This adds an in-game config menu and generates files in ' _.minecraft/config/_'.

[< Common's _Config Code_ >](https://github.com/Serilum/Collective/tree/HEAD/Common/src/main/java/com/natamus/collective/config)

![](https://cdn.serilum.com/projects/collective/a.png)

![](https://cdn.serilum.com/projects/collective/b.png)

**2** \| Over the years, I've added lots of useful code to Collective. Being able to use these makes my life of updating dependent mods a lot easier:

[< Common's _Functions_ >](https://github.com/Serilum/Collective/tree/HEAD/Common/src/main/java/com/natamus/collective/functions)

![](https://cdn.serilum.com/projects/collective/c.png)

**3** \| I've released bundles of my mods for easier downloading!

Collective allows enabling/disabling the included mods via some neat code!

[< Fabric's _Bundle Code_ >](https://github.com/Serilum/Collective/tree/HEAD/Fabric/src/main/java/com/natamus/collective/fabric/bundle)

![](https://cdn.serilum.com/projects/collective/d.png)

**4** \| Access transformers/wideners are used to set and use fields Mojang has made private. Having these in Collective keeps everything organised:

[< Fabric's _collective.accesswidener_ >](https://github.com/Serilum/Collective/blob/HEAD/Common/src/main/resources/collective.accesswidener)

![](https://cdn.serilum.com/projects/collective/e.png)

**5** \| See the full source code here:

[**https://github.com/Serilum/Collective**](https://github.com/Serilum/Collective)

![Notes and links](https://cdn.serilum.com/description/nameplate/notes-n-links.svg)

**You may freely use this mod in any modpack, as long as the download remains hosted within the CurseForge or Modrinth ecosystem.**

[Serilum.com](https://www.curseforge.com/linkout?remoteUrl=https%253a%252f%252fserilum.com%252f) contains an overview and more information on all mods available.

Comments are disabled as I'm unable to keep track of them across so many separate mod pages.

For issues, ideas, suggestions or anything else there is the [Github repo](https://github.com/Serilum/.issue-tracker). Thanks!

## Fabric API is the core library for the most common hooks and inter-compatibility measures utilized by mods using the Fabric toolchain.

- Fabric’s APIs are lightweight and modular, making porting faster and game instances leaner.
- Fabric development targets snapshots as well as release versions, allowing earlier mod updates and more informed community planning.
- The Fabric toolchain is available for everyone to use - even if you only want to use some of it!

### **Installation**

Fabric comes in two parts:

- Fabric Loader: Minecraft version independent, provides the essentials of mod loading and rudimentary modding
- Fabric API: Minecraft version specific, a mod like any other, provides all sorts of APIs  for interoperability and convenience (this CurseForge project)

Instructions:

1. Install Fabric Loader from the [Fabric website](https://www.curseforge.com/linkout?remoteUrl=https%253a%252f%252ffabricmc.net%252f) \- there is an installer for the vanilla launcher and dedicated servers, other launchers including the Curse App may do this automatically

2. Optionally try to run the game to verify the installation and create the mods folder. There should be Fabric related log entries and the main menu will mention Fabric at the bottom next to the Minecraft version.
3. Download Fabric API for the desired Minecraft version from this page and put the jar file in the mods folder like any ordinary mod

More information and full installation instructions can be found on the [Fabric website](https://www.curseforge.com/linkout?remoteUrl=https%253a%252f%252ffabricmc.net%252f) and support is available through the [Fabric discord server](https://discord.gg/v6v4pMv).

**This is SEPARATE from the Fabric loader! You need both for most mods!** **Keep in mind the project requires the Fabric mod loader!**

# RenderLib

- By
[![meldexun](https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/jtv_user_pictures/c26aedbb-9ea2-4a6f-b80e-5de8000236ac-profile_image-150x150.png)meldexun](https://www.curseforge.com/members/meldexun)


Library for entity rendering

Download

- [Description](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/renderlib)
- [Comments (17)](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/renderlib/comments)
- [Files](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/renderlib/files?page=1&pageSize=20&showAlphaFiles=hide)
- [Gallery](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/renderlib/gallery)
- [Relations](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/renderlib/relations/dependencies)
- [Issues](https://github.com/Meldexun/RenderLib/issues)

This mod requires **MixinBootstrap** ( [curseforge](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/mixinbootstrap), [modrinth](https://www.curseforge.com/linkout?remoteUrl=https%253a%252f%252fmodrinth.com%252fmod%252fmixinbootstrap)) to run!

**Mixin 0.7-0.8 Compatibility** ( [curseforge](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/mixin-0-7-0-8-compatibility), [modrinth](https://www.curseforge.com/linkout?remoteUrl=https%253a%252f%252fmodrinth.com%252fmod%252fmixincompat)) might be helpful when another mod uses an older mixin version and you are thus unable to launch the game.

**RenderLib** is a client-side only mod that makes necessary changes to entity and tile entity rendering for some of my other mods.
This mod on its own does not provide any meaningful improvements regarding performance and you probably only want to install it when using a mod that has this mod as a dependency.

You might want to check out my mods that have this mod as a dependency

- **Entity Culling** ( [curseforge](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/entity-culling), [modrinth](https://www.curseforge.com/linkout?remoteUrl=https%253a%252f%252fmodrinth.com%252fproject%252fentity-culling)) \- Skip rendering of entities that are occluded by blocks
- **Nothirium** ( [curseforge](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/nothirium), [modrinth](https://www.curseforge.com/linkout?remoteUrl=https%253a%252f%252fmodrinth.com%252fproject%252fnothirium) \- Greatly improve FPS by using modern OpenGL for chunk rendering

If you want to use RenderLib along TickDynamic then you should check out this fork of TickDynamic which is compatible with RenderLib: **Tick Dynamic Continuation** ( [curseforge](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/tick-dynamic-continuation), [modrinth](https://www.curseforge.com/linkout?remoteUrl=https%253a%252f%252fmodrinth.com%252fmod%252ftick-dynamic-continuation))
